metaDescription: Six waterproof latex coated gardening gloves compared on coating depth, liner, winter warmth, pack size and grip for wet soil, mud and cold weather.
introParagraphs: Waterproof is a promise that deserves a careful look, because a glove can keep out water in three quite different ways. Some are knit liners dipped only on the palm, which keeps the palm dry but lets water wick in through the back. Some are coated over the whole hand, which blocks water but also blocks air. And a few add a fleece lining for cold, wet mornings. Which one you need depends on whether you are dealing with damp soil, a hose, or an early frost.

The six pairs here are all latex coated. The COOLJOB double-coated glove and the KAYGO KG150 are lightweight waterproof work gloves with a double latex layer, and the Schwer is a double-latex pair with a stated ANSI A2 cut level and a warmer feel. The Mimorou is a 12-pair bulk pack, the generic natural latex glove has a three-quarter waterproof coating, and the COOLJOB winter glove adds a fleece-like inner for cold weather.

We evaluated each pair from its listing specifications and buyer feedback themes, so each coating and lining is as the maker describes it. A waterproof label describes the coated area, and cuffs can still let water in, so we point out where each glove leaves gaps.

products.name: COOLJOB Waterproof Double Rubber Coated Gardening Work Gloves
specs: Double latex on palm and fingers

specList.label: Coating
specList.value: Fully waterproof latex, double layer on palm and fingers

products.description:
The COOLJOB double-coated glove is the most balanced waterproof pick. The listing describes a fully waterproof latex coating that keeps hands clean and dry, with tough double latex on the palm and fingers for added wear, over a soft 15 gauge polyester base the maker calls breathable and dexterous enough for small and oily parts.

The fully coated hand is the important feature. Many so-called waterproof gloves are palm-dipped only, and water seeps in through the knit back the first time you reach into wet grass. A full coating means rain, hose spray and wet soil bounce off the entire hand, which is what you want for jobs like washing planters or digging in a damp bed. The 15 gauge base is thin enough to keep your fingers sensitive, which is rare for a glove that is truly sealed.

Sealed gloves trade breathability for dryness, so your hand will feel clammy on a warm day. The cuff is still open, so water can run down your arm and inside. Compared with the KAYGO, it has a very similar construction, and compared with the Schwer it is thinner and cooler. Rinse it after use and dry it inside out to prevent odor.
products.bestFor: Wet soil, hosing and rainy chores when a fully sealed but still nimble glove is needed.
pros: Double latex on palm and fingers
Thin base keeps good finger feel
cons: Open cuff lets water run in

products.name: KAYGO KG150 Waterproof Double Latex Coated Work Gloves
specs: Waterproof on palm, back and fingers

specList.label: Coating
specList.value: Double latex, palms, backs and fingers

products.description:
The KAYGO KG150 follows a similar recipe with a different emphasis. The listing says the double latex coating keeps the palms, backs and fingers waterproof and flexible in wet conditions, and that sandy latex technology gives a slip-resistant grip on wet, oily or dry surfaces. It is described as lightweight and durable, for gardening, construction, fishing, cleaning and painting.

Sandy texture is a clever solution for the oldest problem of wet gloves: a smooth rubber surface turns into a slippery film once it meets water or soil. The rough finish gives the latex something to bite with, which helps when you hold wet pots, pull stubborn weeds or lift hose reels. A waterproof back is a real advantage over palm-dipped gloves, because it stops water from soaking through when you reach into a stream of runoff.

The KAYGO is not insulated, so it will feel cold on a frosty morning, and its latex needs the same care as any rubber. Next to the COOLJOB double-coated glove, the KAYGO emphasizes grip texture over base breathability, and next to the Schwer it is lighter. Rinse mud off promptly, dry it away from heat and check the coating for cracks each season.
products.bestFor: Handling wet pots, hoses and slippery tools where a textured grip matters.
pros: Double latex coating is waterproof end to end
Sandy texture grips wet and oily items
Waterproof back as well as palm

products.name: Schwer 2 Pairs Waterproof Double Latex Work Gloves CR3306
specs: ANSI A2 cut resistant per listing
products.description:
The Schwer CR3306 adds a few things the other waterproof gloves lack. The listing says it is made without PFAS, has a double-layer latex coating that is waterproof and windproof across the whole hand, a foam latex palm for grip in wet or dry conditions, ANSI A2 cut resistance and a warmer feel. It is sold as two pairs.

A windproof layer is the feature that stands out in cold weather, since wind through a knit glove chills your hands faster than damp does. Combined with enhanced warmth, it makes this the pair to reach for in late autumn or early spring when you are clearing leaves or lifting bulbs. The foam latex palm holds wet tools without a death grip. The A2 cut level is modest, but it is more than you get from the other waterproof pairs and a nice buffer against sharp edges in a shed.

A warmer glove is a hotter glove in summer, and a thicker one limits dexterity compared with the COOLJOB. Compared with the winter COOLJOB, the Schwer has a cut rating and a PFAS-free claim but no fleece lining mentioned. A2 is not a thorn rating. Wash it as the maker advises and dry it in a ventilated place.
products.bestFor: Cold, wet and windy chores where warmth and a stated cut level are both wanted.
pros: Foam latex palm for wet grip

products.name: COOLJOB Winter Waterproof Gardening Work Gloves with Fleece Inner

specList.label: Palm
specList.value: Sandy latex on palm and fingers

products.description:
The COOLJOB winter glove is the one to buy for months when the soil is cold and wet. The listing describes a waterproof and windproof latex coating to block cold air and water, durable sandy latex on the palm and fingers, an extra soft terry inner that keeps hands warm in freezing weather and a snug polyester base. It is sold as a single pair in gift packaging.

A terry or fleece inner changes the day. Cold hands lose dexterity quickly, and a glove with a warm lining lets you keep working at pruning, mulching or digging frozen ground. The sealed latex outer is useful in that situation too, because wet and cold together is the worst combination. The sandy grip keeps tools secure even if frost makes handles slick.

Warmth is not free. The glove is thicker than the summer COOLJOB, and sweat gets trapped in the lining if you wear it in mild weather. Compared with the Schwer, it is a single pair with a fleece-like lining rather than a cut rating. Let it dry fully inside between uses, because a damp lining feels colder than no glove at all.
products.bestFor: Cold, wet work in autumn and winter when a lined waterproof glove is needed.

products.name: Generic Waterproof Thorn-Proof Natural Latex Gardening Gloves
products.description:
This unbranded natural latex glove sits at the thin, flexible end of the lineup. The listing describes treated natural latex with a second-skin fit for men and women, reinforced padding on the palms and fingertips, and a three-quarter waterproof coating that blocks mud and moisture to keep hands and nails dry. The color is grey.

The key phrase is three-quarter coating, which means the palm and fingers are covered but the back of the hand and part of the cuff are not fully sealed. That makes the glove breathable and nimble, and it suits planting, weeding and rose-bed work where you want finger feel but still want protection from damp soil. The reinforced padding on the palms and fingertips adds a margin against sharp twigs, though the listing's thorn claim is a statement of intent, not a rating.

Because it is not fully waterproof, it is the wrong glove for submerged jobs, and because it is unbranded, the listing is less specific about sizing and construction. Compared with the COOLJOB double-coated glove, it is less sealed and more flexible. Compared with the Mimorou, it is a single, tailored pair. Rinse it, dry it away from heat and check for tears around the fingertips.
products.bestFor: Planting and weeding in damp soil when finger feel matters more than full sealing.
pros: Coating keeps mud off hands and nails
Breathes better than a full coating

products.name: Mimorou 12 Pairs Waterproof Work Gloves Double Coated Rubber
products.description:
The Mimorou is a big pack of twelve pairs of blue double-coated waterproof gloves, aimed at people who go through gloves quickly. The listing says the double latex coating resists liquid, the textured surface helps grip tools such as shovels, brooms and scissors, and the gloves fit both women and men. The size listed here is medium.

A dozen pairs changes how you treat gloves. Waterproof work is rough on coatings, and a glove that is torn at the thumb is no longer waterproof. With a bulk pack you can keep pairs in the car, the shed, the kitchen and the garage, hand them to helpers and throw a pair away when the fingertip splits. For a community garden, a family project or a spring cleanup, that practicality is the whole point.

Bulk packs usually trade quality control for quantity, so expect some variation in fit and coating thickness. Compared with the COOLJOB double-coated glove, the Mimorou is a more disposable approach, and next to the Schwer it lacks a cut rating. Check the first pair for sizing, rinse used gloves and discard any with cracks in the latex.
products.bestFor: Group projects and households that go through waterproof gloves quickly.
pros: Twelve pairs for many users or locations
cons: No cut rating or warmth claims

buyingCriteria.explanation: A palm-dip keeps the palm dry and lets water soak through the back. The COOLJOB double-coated glove and the KAYGO coat the hand fully, and the generic natural latex glove uses a three-quarter coating. Choose a full coating for hosing and rain, and a partial one for damp soil where breathability matters. Check the listing for words like backs and fingers, because they signal how far the coating goes.

Even a sealed glove lets water in at the open cuff. Gloves with an elastic cuff, such as the winter COOLJOB, keep spray out better than loose ones. Tucking the glove under a rain jacket sleeve stops runoff, but tucking it over lets water drip in. Consider the cuff as part of the waterproofing, not an afterthought.

Wet and cold together strip heat from the hand faster than either alone. The winter COOLJOB adds a terry inner, and the Schwer is windproof with a warmer feel. The thin KAYGO and summer COOLJOB offer no insulation. If you work below about freezing, choose a lined glove and carry a dry spare.

A wet latex surface can feel like soap, and texture is the fix. The KAYGO uses sandy latex, the winter COOLJOB uses sandy latex on the palm and fingers, and the Schwer uses foam latex. Run a thumb across the palm in the listing photos, because a smooth coating will slip. Good grip lets you hold a tool without squeezing.

Waterproof does not mean tough. The Schwer states an ANSI A2 cut level, which is modest, and the other gloves state no rating. Thorns and nails can puncture a thin latex layer, so do not rely on these for rose pruning. Keep a leather glove for thorny work and a waterproof one for wet tasks.

Some people react to natural latex, and the COOLJOB, KAYGO, Schwer, Mimorou and generic gloves all use it. Look at a thin liner glove if you notice skin irritation, and consider an alternative material. Rinse latex after use and keep it out of sunlight and heat, since both break it down over time. A pair stored crumpled in a hot truck will crack at the finger creases within a season.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water exclusion
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how much of the hand each glove seals. The COOLJOB double-coated glove, KAYGO, Schwer and winter COOLJOB are described as waterproof across the hand, the Mimorou has a double coating, and the generic glove uses a three-quarter coating. Open cuffs limit all of them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warmth
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted gloves by insulation claims. The winter COOLJOB with its terry inner leads, the Schwer follows with a windproof, warmer build, and the thin pairs offer none. Cold climates change the ranking more than anything else.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip when wet
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered texture. The KAYGO sandy latex, the winter COOLJOB sandy latex palm and the Schwer foam latex palm lead, with the Mimorou textured surface following. Smooth coatings are weaker when wet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dexterity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared base thickness. The COOLJOB double-coated glove with its 15 gauge base and the generic second-skin glove lead, the KAYGO follows, and the Schwer and winter COOLJOB are thicker. A thin glove is easier for planting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and replacement
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pack sizes. The Mimorou 12-pair pack and Schwer two-pair pack lead for volume, while the COOLJOB gloves are sold in single or small packs. Waterproof coatings wear out, so spares matter.

faq.q: Are waterproof gardening gloves really waterproof?
faq.a: The coated area is waterproof, but the cuff is open, and water can run inside. Fully coated gloves like the COOLJOB double-coated and KAYGO seal the hand, while the generic glove seals the palm and fingers. Tuck your sleeve over the cuff when working under spray.

faq.q: Why do my hands sweat in waterproof gloves?
faq.a: A sealed coating blocks moisture in both directions, so perspiration cannot escape. Choose a thin breathable base, such as the 15 gauge COOLJOB, and take breaks to air your hands. A three-quarter coating helps in warm weather.

faq.q: Can I use these gloves for thorny plants?
faq.a: Not as your main protection. Latex coatings are thin, and thorns can puncture them. Use a leather glove for roses and brambles and keep these for wet, muddy jobs.

faq.q: How do I clean latex coated gloves?
faq.a: Rinse off mud, wash gently with mild soap and let them air dry away from direct heat or sun. Turn them inside out if the lining is damp. Avoid solvents, which can weaken the latex.

faq.q: What if I am allergic to latex?
faq.a: Natural latex can irritate sensitive skin, and these gloves use latex coatings. Consider a nitrile coated alternative, or wear a thin liner underneath. If you notice a reaction, stop using the gloves and ask a doctor.

faq.q: Do winter gloves work in summer?
faq.a: They will feel hot, because the lining traps heat. The winter COOLJOB suits temperatures near freezing. Use a thinner pair such as the KAYGO or generic latex glove for mild weather.

faq.q: How long do waterproof coatings last?
faq.a: They wear fastest on the thumb, forefinger and palm, especially with rough tools. Latex also degrades with sun and heat. Replace a glove when the coating cracks or peels, since it will no longer keep water out.
